items.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003
items.q: my Uncle Ben... befriended Hoagy Carmichael. In fact my Uncle Ben always told me that the major part of the song “Stardust” was his. And Hoagy was very close to my uncle for all of his life.

ctx.x: You have had a marvelous career in different parts of the music. And I’m wondering if when you were a boy or a young man at what point did you set your career path? Is it possible — was it that definite of a time?

Well I think that there are little pivot points that sort of set the tone for what my destiny — if I can use that word — was to be. I think my spiritual values came from the time that I was an altar boy in the African Methodist Episcopal Church. My brother and I, my brother that’s next to me, we were both at an early age, seven years old or something like that. And my mother was originally a Baptist so I came up through that whole African- American tradition of Baptist church and then the African-American…
gentleman who befriended Hoagy Carmichael. In fact my Uncle Ben always told me that the major part of the song “Stardust” was his.
